chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And feed the desperate one, the poor.' He said: 'He is the chronically ill person who is unable to go out due to his chronic illness.'

key_terms.الزَّمِنُ: The chronically ill person; one suffering from a long-term ailment
key_terms.الْبَائِسَ: The desperate one; a specific category of poor person, here defined as chronically ill

ai.seo_question: Who is considered the 'desperate one' (al-ba'is) in the context of Quranic charity?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) clarifies that the term 'al-ba'is' (desperate one) in Surah Al-Hajj specifically refers to the chronically ill (al-zamin) who are confined to their homes due to their condition. This interpretation highlights a nuanced understanding of social welfare in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that charity must extend beyond general poverty to include those physically incapacitated from seeking sustenance.
